record.context_brief: Inhomogeneous minima of indefinite binary quadratic forms
record.original_question: For any nondegenerate indefinite binary quadratic form Q with rational coefficients that does not represent zero over Q, is the supremum m(Q) rational and isolated, and are both m(Q) and m2(Q) attained at points with coordinates in the splitting field of Q?

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 46 (E. Barnes, H. Swinnerton-Dyer [11]). For any quadratic form Q as above, the supremum m(Q) is rational and isolated. Both m (Q) and m2(Q) are attained at points with coordinates in the the splitting ﬁel d of Q.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Q(x,y) = ax^2 + bxy + cy^2$ be a nondegenerate indefinite binary quadratic form with rational coefficients (so $a,b,c \in \mathbb{Q}$, the discriminant $b^2 - 4ac > 0$, and $b^2 - 4ac$ is not a rational square), and assume $Q$ does not represent zero over $\mathbb{Q}$ (equivalently, $Q(x,y) = 0$ has no nontrivial rational solution). Define the inhomogeneous minimum function on $\mathbb{R}^2$ by
$$M_Q(\alpha,\beta) \;=\; \inf_{(x,y) \in \mathbb{Z}^2} |Q(x+\alpha,\, y+\beta)|,$$
and set
$$m(Q) \;=\; \sup_{(\alpha,\beta)\in \mathbb{R}^2} M_Q(\alpha,\beta), \qquad m_2(Q) \;=\; \sup\bigl\{ M_Q(\alpha,\beta) : (\alpha,\beta) \notin \Sigma(Q) \bigr\},$$
where $\Sigma(Q)$ denotes the set of pairs $(\alpha,\beta) \in \mathbb{R}^2$ at which $M_Q$ achieves the global supremum $m(Q)$. Let $K_Q$ denote the splitting field of $Q$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, i.e. the real quadratic field $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{b^2-4ac})$.

Prove or disprove the following:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $m(Q) \in \mathbb{Q}$ and $m(Q)$ is isolated in the sense that $m(Q) > m_2(Q)$.
\item Both suprema $m(Q)$ and $m_2(Q)$ are attained, and they are attained at points $(\alpha,\beta) \in \mathbb{R}^2$ whose coordinates lie in $K_Q$.
\end{enumerate}
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture, due to E. S. Barnes and H. P. F. Swinnerton-Dyer from their 1950s series on inhomogeneous minima of binary quadratic forms, remains a long-standing open problem. Partial results exist for individual forms and small discriminants (Barnes–Swinnerton-Dyer I–III, and later work, e.g. Sawyer, Ennola, and Gruber), but no general proof of rationality, isolation, and attainment in the splitting field is known. Recent surveys of open problems in dynamics still list it as open.
